3.sheetLine: You are standing at a door that already closed.

4.tense: It is being built, the work is being done, and you are telling the story as if it were happening to someone else.
4.verb: Building something new from what the clearing revealed
4.place: Standing where what you are becomes visible
4.ask: A direction you chose is about to be questioned — by someone, or by your own doubt. When it comes, hold the heading without arguing for it. Not the whole fight; just the next push.
4.core:
Something is being raised here, and you are not counting yourself among the hands that raise it. The skill, the timing, the quiet decision underneath — those are being described as circumstance or chance, anything but yours. You are steering, but not looking at the wheel.

The thing already built knows your name. Take a direction you have already chosen — not a new one — and hold it against the next pressure to bend. That is not stubbornness; it is keeping the heading when it is contested. You do not need to announce it or explain it to anyone. The resolve that has been carrying you forward is yours, and seeing that is the beginning of becoming what you already are.
4.sheetLine: You are building it and refusing the credit.

1.tense: A whole shape is opening up here, and your hands are already on the first piece of it.
1.verb: raising the first structure that wasn't there before
1.place: seeing the whole pattern at once, from inside it
1.ask: Take a piece of work you've come to know well and walk a person through it start to finish, naming each turn as you reach it, then let go of what they do next.
1.core:
You can hold a whole shape and still work on the first piece of it. That combination is what makes what you raise stand up — you keep checking the build against what is actually on the table, not against the picture you started with.

Take a piece of work you've come to know well and walk a person through it start to finish, naming each turn as you reach it, then let go of what they do next. A route spoken through once is enough for most; theirs may look different from yours, and that is fine. What you raised stops belonging to you alone and becomes something another person can stand on.
1.sheetLine: You hold the whole shape and your hands know the first piece.

2.tense: You're raising the far end of a shape whose middle nobody has stood in yet.
2.verb: raising the first structure that wasn't there before
2.place: seeing the whole pattern at once, from inside it
2.ask: Name a standing arrangement you keep up out of habit, skip the next two, and put that time into something shared that still has life in it.
2.core:
The whole structure is going up before any of it has been tried by use. You read the pattern and you're already nailing down the end that doesn't exist yet, settling questions before anyone has raised them. Set alongside what's already moving, your version looks finished in a way nothing new can be.

Something you keep up has gone hollow as a place to meet. Name a standing arrangement you keep up out of habit, skip the next two, and put that time into something shared that still has life in it. Your read of the shape may turn out mostly right. The part you got wrong only shows up once you're standing among the others rather than over them, and you can afford to find it.
2.sheetLine: You're building the end before anyone's used the middle.

3.tense: The shape was plain once, and you are still standing where it came clear.
3.verb: raising the first structure that wasn't there before
3.place: seeing the whole pattern at once, from inside it
3.ask: Settle one small question you've been holding open, and do the first piece of it before today ends. No explaining the choice to anyone.
3.core:
You saw the pattern. That part happened, and it was clear. Since then you've been standing in that spot, holding the whole plan, and nothing has been built from it. Any move might break it, so none is made, and the pieces stay where the drawing put them. From outside it looks like you withdrew; from inside it feels like you are still deciding.

Settle one small question you've been holding open, and do the first piece of it before today ends. No explaining the choice to anyone. Not the whole structure — a first piece. Perceiving the pattern was the start rather than the finished work, and the way through is something your feet can find again.
3.sheetLine: You saw the whole shape and haven't started it.

4.tense: A shape is being held together by your hands while you describe yourself as only watching.
4.verb: raising the first structure that wasn't there before
4.place: seeing the whole pattern at once, from inside it
4.ask: When disagreement lands on a direction you picked, wait one beat before answering, then stay with what you chose; leave the choice unexplained for now.
4.core:
A shape is being held together right now, and the one holding it is you. You read what's happening across the layers earlier than anyone standing near you, and you act on what you read — quietly, without announcing it. Ask how it holds, and the answer is that you're only watching, that the thing keeps itself up. The work is authored. The author isn't signing.

When disagreement lands on a direction you picked, wait one beat before answering, then stay with what you chose; leave the choice unexplained for now. Not a defense — the heading, kept. What you picked was picked for a reason, and the picking happened in your own hands.
4.sheetLine: You're holding it together and calling it watching.

1.tense: The structure is going up now and the hands are still on it.
1.verb: building something new from what the clearing left standing
1.place: the threshold where finished work becomes the next beginning
1.ask: With one person stuck at the point you already got past, put the route down in plain words and then go quiet about it — no doubling back to check.
1.core:
You're at the part where work gets finished well enough to leave your hands. It's going without strain, because you're trusting the form to hold rather than guarding it. What you built is integrated, and the finishing opens instead of closing. New structure is emerging in how you think about the work, the first frame of it, and it comes out of the hands-on part rather than the plans.

The way back moves through other people, and it looks like plain direction. You spent real effort learning this route; someone behind you on the same stretch hasn't. Put down where the passage is and go quiet. The telling won't thin you — solitude on the way back connects instead of isolating, and refining your own work could turn into gripping. Here it doesn't, because you're willing to hand it on.
1.sheetLine: What you built is finished enough to leave your hands.

2.tense: The finished version is being lived in already, ahead of the hands.
2.verb: building something new from what the clearing left standing
2.place: the threshold where finished work becomes the next beginning
2.ask: Drop the piece you keep re-adding out of habit, even though nobody living uses it — take it out of the next version by your own hand.
2.core:
You're at the crossing point and already living past it. The final form is in your head, so the raising feels behind schedule and the hands get pushed past what the thing can hold. What you're defending isn't the work; it's a shape that hasn't arrived. The last step keeps getting thrown over the top of the one under it.

What brings you back is going toward the connection that's still live — the people this is actually for — and letting the rest fall away. The piece you keep adding because it was once right, or because cutting it feels like loss, is the piece that no longer travels. Take out one of those by your own hand and watch what the live connection does with the space that opens.
2.sheetLine: You're finishing it in your head before it's built.

3.tense: The old structures came down and nothing new has risen since.
3.verb: building something new from what the clearing left standing
3.place: the threshold where finished work becomes the next beginning
3.ask: Make the next call on this build and carry it through before the day ends — nobody is told, nobody is given a reason.
3.core:
You can see the cleared ground and you stand at the far side of it. The old structures came down — you know exactly where they were — and nothing is going up on the space. You can describe what should be raised; you just don't start. The not-starting has gone on long enough that it feels like judgment rather than fear.

What's called for doesn't require you to feel like building. Make the call and carry it through the same day. Small, no announcement, no reasons given to anybody. Real authority doesn't assert itself — it moves, and the structure does the talking. This first move doesn't have to be right. It has to be made, because making it is the only thing that puts ground back under your feet.
3.sheetLine: You can see the cleared ground. Nothing's rising on it.

4.tense: The build is underway and your telling credits it to circumstance.
4.verb: building something new from what the clearing left standing
4.place: the threshold where finished work becomes the next beginning
4.ask: Somebody questions where this is going — let the course stand exactly as it is, through that conversation, without mounting a case for it.
4.core:
You're building, and you credit the build to luck. Asked how it came together, you say it came together — you had the opportunity, the pieces happened to fit. Meanwhile the direction is genuinely yours: the choices, the order of them, the refusal of the easier shape. Your hand decided. Your account of it leaves the hand out.

What's needed is older than you think. Before the build there was a want — a pull toward a particular thing that the structure now carries — and it's still what moves you when you let it. Feel for what you actually want here and keep the heading from there. Momentum isn't gathered by pushing; it's harvested from engagement. What you're engaged with has been yours the whole time.
4.sheetLine: The build is yours, and your telling leaves the hand out.
